conventions.convention: The trapezoidal rule uses N ≥ 1 equal panels, h=(b−a)/N, half-weight endpoints, and an empty interior sum equal to zero when N=1.
The Gaussian quadratic-form integral is a nonnegative Lebesgue integral in dimension d ≥ 1, with real symmetric positive-definite H and Countable Choice assumed.

The Laplace theorem uses H=−D²h at the unique interior global maximum, positive integer n tending to infinity, and asymptotic equivalence meaning ratio convergence to one; it asserts no relative O(n⁻¹) remainder.
The interpolation lemma assumes C² regularity on an open neighborhood of the closed interval.

The composite trapezoidal error theorem instead admits C²([a,b]) with one-sided endpoint derivatives and uses the Riemann integral; its proof constructs a C² extension before applying the interpolation lemma.

alerts.finding: cex-local-hessian-does-not-capture-multiple-modes places 'A nondegenerate local Hessian at one mode does not by itself ensure that a one-mode Laplace Gaussian approximates the full posterior law in total variation, even when the full-data model identifies the parameter.' under '## Statement refuted'. This is the true conclusion established by its counterexample, rather than the assertion being refuted. The heading and logical polarity disagree; its citation of the Laplace theorem's unique-global-maximum hypothesis is faithful.
